quotes.text: If your first API uses OAuth and your second uses API keys, you haven't gained flexibility. You have created inconsistency, and that inconsistency is a massive security liability.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why per-API freedom turns into a security problem.

quotes.text: The real cost of your backend isn't the initial build. It is the maintenance burden that grows silently until you are spending half your engineering capacity just to keep the lights on.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes backend cost as long-term maintenance rather than build effort.

quotes.text: An agent doesn't have permissions. The API it calls has permissions. The agent is just a consumer, like any other.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp security principle for agentic applications.

quotes.text: Rayfin only solves your custom API problems if you take the time to govern it correctly. If you don't, you haven't actually solved the problem. You have just shifted it to a new tool.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns that self-service backends without guardrails simply create a new kind of sprawl.

quotes.text: The technology is the easy part, changing how your organization actually works is the hard part and to be honest, it is going to hurt.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the organizational change as the real challenge of platform adoption.

chapters.title: Why custom APIs became a liability

takeaways: Fragmented custom APIs scatter authentication, monitoring and governance across many systems, which makes them a growing liability, especially for AI agents.
Rayfin defines the whole backend in code, deploys it into Microsoft Fabric and enforces access policies, masking and audit trails by default.
Adopt it gradually with a pilot domain, a facade and an anti-corruption layer, backed by templates, a governance library and a governance board.
hook: Front ends can now be built in an afternoon, but the backend behind them still takes weeks of custom API plumbing. This episode explains for architects and platform teams how Microsoft Rayfin turns the backend into governed code inside Microsoft Fabric, why that matters for AI agents, and how to migrate away from custom APIs step by step.
